blocks.text: Agentic SOC incidents are designed to quickly provide complete context for all incidents and to let you pivot to specific asset information for deeper insights, enabling your Security Operations Center (SOC) team to make faster, more effective decisions. When you open the Incidents page, it provides high-level information at a glance about the incidents affecting your organization, and you can merge, sort, update, and add comments to the incidents listed in the table. To learn how to investigate and remediate an incident, see Viewing Incident Details.
The Incidents page provides the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: View high-level data measuring the impact of all incidents.
Use charts and graphs to quickly learn about the impact of all incidents.
Filter and sort incidents based on severity, data source, time range, and more.
Make bulk edits and exports.
Save filters (custom views) of incidents most important to you.

blocks.text: On the Incidents page (Agentic SOC > Incidents), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Select from system-saved views, or views you previously saved.
Search for specific incidents by entering keywords in the search bar.
Save your view for quick access after making adjustments to it (e.g., applying filters, adjusting columns, grouping).
Filter the incident information on the page, and add new filters to control the information you see.
See the number of incidents by status, severity, and verdict, displayed as charts.
Modify multiple incidents at once, such as updating the status, merging incidents together, and adding comments.
Specify grouping for the incidents in the table (e.g., incident first seen, incident last seen, incident tags).
Refresh table data, export table data to a CSV file, and configure the columns displayed in the table.
View a list of all incidents affecting your organization. The table displays the following columns by default:
ID: The ID number of the incident.
Severity: The severity of the incident (e.g., Critical, High, Medium).
Type: The type of incident (e.g., AI, Platform, Custom).
Title: The title of the incident.
Created: The date the incident was created.
Alerts Count: The number of alerts associated with the incident.
Sources: The sources of the threat data (e.g., threats identified from Zscaler logs are identified by the Zscaler logo, threats identified from third-party apps are identified by app logos).
Assignee: The user assigned to the incident.
Status: The status of the incident (e.g., Discovered, Confirmed, Closed).
Verdict: The verdict for the incident (e.g., Malicious, Suspicious, Benign).

blocks.text: For each incident in the list, you can click to see a detailed view of data about that incident. You can also customize the detailed view for incidents. To learn more, see Customizing Alert and Incident Detail Pages.
